title: Industrial radiography licensing, records and notifications practice questions
description: Practice questions on NRC 10 CFR Part 34: scope, definitions, license applications, record form and location, and incident notifications.

questions.question: Which use of byproduct material does 34.1 say Part 34 does not apply to?

options.A: Sealed sources used at temporary jobsites
options.B: Medical uses of byproduct material
options.C: Sealed sources used in offshore platform radiography
options.D: Sealed sources stored at field stations

questions.explanation: 34.1 states: "This rule does not apply to medical uses of byproduct material."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.1, Purpose and scope (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This rule does not apply to medical uses of byproduct material.

questions.question: Apart from what the Commission specifically authorizes in writing, whose written interpretation of Part 34 does 34.5 recognize as binding upon the Commission?

options.A: The licensee's Radiation Safety Officer for industrial radiography
options.B: An independent certifying organization
options.C: The radiographer in charge at the jobsite
options.D: The General Counsel

questions.explanation: 34.5 recognizes no interpretation by an NRC officer or employee as binding "other than a written interpretation by the General Counsel."
questions.evidence: other than a written interpretation by the General Counsel, will be recognized to be binding upon the Commission

questions.question: How does 34.3 define a permanent radiographic installation?

options.A: An enclosed shielded room, cell, or vault, not located at a temporary jobsite, in which radiography is performed
options.B: A facility where licensed material may be stored or used and from which equipment is dispatched
options.C: Any vehicle that is locked and used to secure a radiographic exposure device when it is not in use
options.D: A location where radiographic operations are conducted other than the locations of use authorized on the license

questions.explanation: 34.3: "Permanent radiographic installation means an enclosed shielded room, cell, or vault, not located at a temporary jobsite, in which radiography is performed."
questions.evidence: Permanent radiographic installation means an enclosed shielded room, cell, or vault, not located at a temporary jobsite, in which radiography is performed.

questions.question: A licensee's crew performs radiography at a customer's plant that is not one of the locations of use authorized on the license. What does 34.3 call this kind of location?

options.A: A field station
options.B: A permanent radiographic installation
options.C: A temporary jobsite
options.D: A storage area

questions.explanation: 34.3 defines a temporary jobsite as "a location where radiographic operations are conducted and where licensed material may be stored other than those location(s) of use authorized on the license."
questions.evidence: Temporary jobsite means a location where radiographic operations are conducted and where licensed material may be stored other than those location(s) of use authorized on the license.

questions.question: Which activity does the 34.3 definition of radiographic operations expressly include?

options.A: Transport of the device by a common or contract transport
options.B: Filing the license application on NRC Form 313
options.C: Surveys to confirm the adequacy of boundaries
options.D: Medical uses of byproduct material

questions.explanation: Radiographic operations include activities during use or transport "(except when being transported by a common or contract transport), to include surveys to confirm the adequacy of boundaries, setting up equipment and any activity inside restricted area boundaries."
questions.evidence: to include surveys to confirm the adequacy of boundaries, setting up equipment and any activity inside restricted area boundaries

questions.question: What other names does 34.3 give for a radiographic exposure device?

options.A: A camera, or a projector
options.B: A source changer, or a storage container
options.C: A collimator, or an exposure head
options.D: A source stop, or a guide tube

questions.explanation: 34.3 defines the "Radiographic exposure device (also called a camera, or a projector)".
questions.evidence: Radiographic exposure device (also called a camera, or a projector)

questions.question: Under 34.3, which device is designed and used for replacement of sealed sources in radiographic exposure devices?

options.A: A storage container
options.B: A collimator
options.C: A control (drive) cable
options.D: A source changer

questions.explanation: 34.3: "Source changer means a device designed and used for replacement of sealed sources in radiographic exposure devices, including those also used for transporting and storage of sealed sources."
questions.evidence: Source changer means a device designed and used for replacement of sealed sources in radiographic exposure devices

questions.question: Which unit does 34.3 define as the SI unit of absorbed dose, equal to 100 rads?

options.A: The sievert
options.B: The gray
options.C: The becquerel
options.D: The roentgen

questions.explanation: 34.3: "Gray means the SI unit of absorbed dose." It adds: "It is also equal to 100 rads."
questions.evidence: Gray means the SI unit of absorbed dose. One gray is equal to an absorbed dose of 1 Joule/kilogram. It is also equal to 100 rads.

questions.question: According to 34.3, what does the acronym ALARA stand for?

options.A: As low as is reasonably achievable
options.B: As low as radiologically allowable
options.C: Always limit and record all activity
options.D: Annual limit as recorded annually

questions.explanation: 34.3 defines "ALARA (acronym for “as low as is reasonably achievable”)".
questions.evidence: ALARA (acronym for “as low as is reasonably achievable”)

questions.question: On what does 34.11 say a person may file an application for a specific license for use of sealed sources in industrial radiography?

options.A: An application to an independent certifying organization
options.B: A written report to the Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards
options.C: A notice to the appropriate NRC regional office under 34.101(c)
options.D: NRC Form 313, “Application for Material License”

questions.explanation: A person "may file an application for specific license for use of sealed sources in industrial radiography on NRC Form 313, “Application for Material License,”".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.11, Application for a specific license (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: may file an application for specific license for use of sealed sources in industrial radiography on NRC Form 313, “Application for Material License,”

questions.question: Under 34.13(j), the applicant identifies and describes the location(s) of which facilities?

options.A: All certifying entities its radiographers have used
options.B: All manufacturers of its radiographic exposure devices
options.C: All field stations and permanent radiographic installations
options.D: All customers it has served in the past year

questions.explanation: 34.13(j): "The applicant identifies and describes the location(s) of all field stations and permanent radiographic installations."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.13, Specific license for industrial radiography (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The applicant identifies and describes the location(s) of all field stations and permanent radiographic installations.

questions.question: An applicant intends to analyze its own wipe samples. Under 34.13(h), what must the application include?

options.A: A letter of approval from the sealed source manufacturer
options.B: A description of the procedures to be followed
options.C: Wipe sample results from another licensee's laboratory
options.D: A certification of the analyst issued by a certifying entity

questions.explanation: 34.13(h): "If the applicant intends to analyze its own wipe samples, the application must include a description of the procedures to be followed."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.13, Specific license for industrial radiography (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the applicant intends to analyze its own wipe samples, the application must include a description of the procedures to be followed.

questions.question: Under 34.13(g), whose qualifications does the applicant identify and list?

options.A: Each customer at its temporary jobsites
options.B: The individual(s) designated as the RSO and potential designees
options.C: The examiners of the certifying entity
options.D: The drivers of any common or contract carrier it uses

questions.explanation: 34.13(g): "The applicant identifies and lists the qualifications of the individual(s) designated as the RSO (§ 34.42) and potential designees".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.13, Specific license for industrial radiography (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The applicant identifies and lists the qualifications of the individual(s) designated as the RSO (§ 34.42) and potential designees

questions.topic: License copies and form of records
questions.question: Under 34.61, until when does a licensee keep a copy of its license, license conditions, documents incorporated by reference, and their amendments?

options.A: For 6 months after each document is issued
options.B: Until the next NRC inspection of the licensee
options.C: Until the Radiation Safety Officer leaves the licensee
options.D: Until superseded by new documents approved by the Commission, or until the Commission terminates the license

questions.explanation: The licensee keeps these items "until superseded by new documents approved by the Commission, or until the Commission terminates the license."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.61, Records of the specific license for industrial radiography (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: until superseded by new documents approved by the Commission, or until the Commission terminates the license

questions.topic: License copies and form of records
questions.question: Under 34.87, a record may be a reproduced copy or a microform provided what?

options.A: The copy or microform is authenticated by authorized personnel and the microform is capable of reproducing a clear copy throughout the required retention period
options.B: The copy or microform is kept at a permanent radiographic installation
options.C: The copy or microform is sent to the NRC regional office each year
options.D: The copy or microform is signed by the radiographer's assistant

questions.explanation: 34.87 allows a copy or microform "provided that the copy or microform is authenticated by authorized personnel and that the microform is capable of reproducing a clear copy throughout the required retention period."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.87, Form of records (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: provided that the copy or microform is authenticated by authorized personnel and that the microform is capable of reproducing a clear copy throughout the required retention period

questions.topic: Where documents and records are kept
questions.question: A crew is working at a temporary jobsite. Which of these does 34.89(b) list among the documents the licensee keeps copies of there?

options.A: The licensee's original application on NRC Form 313
options.B: Records of receipt and transfer of sealed sources under 34.63
options.C: Training and certification records under 34.79
options.D: A copy of 10 CFR parts 19, 20, and 34 of NRC regulations

questions.explanation: 34.89(b) lists documents kept "at each applicable field station and each temporary jobsite," including "A copy of 10 CFR parts 19, 20, and 34 of NRC regulations".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.89, Location of documents and records (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A copy of 10 CFR parts 19, 20, and 34 of NRC regulations;

questions.topic: Where documents and records are kept
questions.question: When a licensee operates under reciprocity pursuant to 150.20, what does 34.89(b) add to the documents kept at each applicable field station and temporary jobsite?

options.A: A copy of the Agreement State's own radiography regulations
options.B: A letter from the NRC regional office approving the work
options.C: A copy of the Agreement State license authorizing the use of licensed materials
options.D: A list of the Agreement State's certifying entities

questions.explanation: 34.89(b)(12): "When operating under reciprocity pursuant to § 150.20 of this chapter, a copy of the Agreement State license authorizing the use of licensed materials."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.89, Location of documents and records (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: When operating under reciprocity pursuant to § 150.20 of this chapter, a copy of the Agreement State license authorizing the use of licensed materials.

questions.question: Which incident involving radiographic equipment does 34.101(a) list as one requiring a written report to the NRC's Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards?

options.A: A scheduled replacement of a sealed source using a source changer
options.B: Unintentional disconnection of the source assembly from the control cable
options.C: A routine calibration of a radiation survey instrument
options.D: A transfer of an exposure device to another licensee

questions.explanation: One listed incident is "Unintentional disconnection of the source assembly from the control cable".
questions.evidence: Unintentional disconnection of the source assembly from the control cable;

questions.question: Which item does 34.101(b) say the licensee shall include in each report submitted under 34.101(a)?

options.A: Qualifications of personnel involved in the incident
options.B: Home addresses of the personnel involved
options.C: Photographs of the jobsite
options.D: A copy of the licensee's training program

questions.explanation: 34.101(b) lists the information for each report, including "Qualifications of personnel involved in the incident."
questions.evidence: Qualifications of personnel involved in the incident.

questions.question: A licensee is storing radioactive material at a location not listed on its license. Under 34.101(c), when must it notify the appropriate NRC regional office?

options.A: Within 30 days after exceeding 180 days in a calendar year
options.B: Prior to exceeding 90 days in a calendar year at that location
options.C: Prior to exceeding 180 days in a calendar year at that location
options.D: Only when the license is renewed

questions.explanation: 34.101(c) applies to a licensee at an unlisted location "for a period in excess of 180 days in a calendar year" and requires notice "prior to exceeding the 180 days."
questions.evidence: shall notify the appropriate NRC regional office listed in § 30.6(b)(2) of this chapter prior to exceeding the 180 days
